Conformity assessment

Certification

Certification can be a useful tool to add credibility, by demonstrating that your product or service meets the expectations of your customers. For some industries, certification is a legal or contractual requirement.

At ISO, we develop International Standards, such as ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. ISO's Committee on Conformity Assessment (CASCO) has produced a number of standards related to the certification process, which are used by certification bodies. Read more about CASCO standards.

Certification – the provision by an independent body of written assurance (a certificate) that the product, service or system in question meets specific requirements.

Accreditation – the formal recognition by an independent body, generally known as an accreditation body, that a certification body operates according to international standards.

Choosing a certification body

When choosing a certification body, you should:

  • Evaluate several certification bodies
  • Check if the certification body uses the relevant CASCO standard
  • Check if it is accredited. Accreditation provides independent confirmation of competence. However, accreditation is not compulsory, and non-accreditation does not necessarily mean the certification body is not reputable. To find an accredited certification body, contact the national accreditation body in your country or visit the International Accreditation Forum’s database CertSearch.
     

How to verify an accredited certification

When seeking to verify a certification issued by an accredited certification body, you can either: 

  • Use the International Accreditation Forum’s global database, IAF CertSearch. CertSearch aggregates data from accreditation bodies and certification bodies, allowing you to confirm certification and accreditation status in one place. Certificates can be verified individually, in bulk, or via API; or
  • Contact the relevant certification body, accreditation body, or Global ACI directly to confirm the respective statuses.

International organizations in cooperation with ISO for accreditation

The Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated (Global ACI) is the international authority on accreditation of laboratories, certification bodies, inspection bodies, proficiency testing providers, validation/verification bodies, reference material producers and biobanks. Its membership includes accreditation bodies, regional cooperation bodies and stakeholder organizations from around the world.

Global ACI provides an internationally recognized accreditation framework that ensures competence, impartiality, and reliability in conformity assessment worldwide. Global ACI has assumed the former roles of the International Accreditation Forum (IAF) and the International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation (ILAC). For more information, please refer to https://global-aci.org/en/home/.

ISO does not perform certification

ISO does not perform certification or issue certificates, and it does not permit anyone to use the ISO logo in connection with certification. Certification is performed by external certification bodies, thus a company or organization cannot be certified by ISO.

Making a complaint in relation to a claim of certification

ISO takes complaints related to the misuse of the ISO logo or false certification to ISO management system standards seriously.

Complaints should be addressed to the certification body that certified the organization. You can identify the certification body by examining the statement of certification, the certification mark used by the organization, or by requesting a copy of the certificate to the ISO standard.

If the above steps cannot be followed, please send us an email with full details of the issue and how we can contact you. While ISO cannot guarantee a resolution or assume any liability, it can help facilitate dialogue between the parties involved and work towards a positive outcome.

If you have identified a false claim of an accredited certification, including misuse of the Global ACI logo, you may inform the Global ACI Secretariat by email.

A response to your complaint will be sent to you within 14 days.

ISO Survey

Find out how many valid certificates there are in each country for the main ISO management system standards.

Can I use the ISO logo?

The ISO logo is a registered trademark and cannot be used by anyone outside of ISO, unless they have been explicitly authorized.

If you wish to use a logo to demonstrate certification, contact the certification body that issued the certificate.

See full details about use of the ISO logo.

Practical solutions for real-world problems

ISO, the International Organization for Standardization, brings global experts together to agree on the best way of doing things – for anything from making a product to managing a process. As one of the oldest non-governmental international organizations, ISO has enabled trade and cooperation between people and companies all over the world since 1946. The International Standards published by ISO serve to make lives easier, safer and better.

26489

International Standards and other deliverables covering almost all aspects of technology, management and manufacturing.

177

Members representing ISO in  their country. There is only one member per country.

843

Technical committees and subcommittees to take care of standards development.

The ISO way

Inclusive

ISO’s consensus-based standards development process ensures that comments from all stakeholders are taken into account

Value-driven

ISO standards serve one purpose: Making lives easier, safer and better. Learn about our vision. 

Independent

Selling our standards allows us to finance their development and maintenance in a neutral environment. 

Can-do

ISO standards are all about identifying the best solutions to global challenges.

Global

ISO members from all regions of the world nominate experts and vote on draft standards. The Central Secretariat coordinates and facilitates broad participation. 

What does ISO mean? 

ISO is the short name for the International Organization for Standardization. It’s not an acronym, but a name inspired by the Greek word isos, meaning “equal” – reflecting our mission to create standards that ensure consistency and equality worldwide. Because the organization’s full name – and its initials – would vary across languages (for example Organisation internationale de normalisation in French), our founders chose “ISO” as a universal short form that could be recognized globally, regardless of language.

Whatever the country, whatever the language, we are always ISO.

<div class="row row-title       " >
<div class="col-md-12"><h2>Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)</h2></div></div><div class="row        " >
<div class="col-md-7"><div class="collapse-link">
        <button class="accordion-button h2 collapsed" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#accordion-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordion-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">General</button>
    </div>
    <div class="collapse ms-4" id="accordion-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
<div class="accordion  faqs" id="id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
    <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-804ed16f-5b2b-4132-8c03-11ec648e2b42"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-804ed16f-5b2b-4132-8c03-11ec648e2b42" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-804ed16f-5b2b-4132-8c03-11ec648e2b42">
            Can anyone join ISO?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-804ed16f-5b2b-4132-8c03-11ec648e2b42" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-804ed16f-5b2b-4132-8c03-11ec648e2b42" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Individuals or businesses can't join ISO. Membership of ISO is only open to national standards institutes or similar organizations that represent standardization in their country (one member in each country). It's important to realize that companies that apply or certify ISO standards are not ISO members. Find out <a href="/about/members" title="Members">more about ISO members.</a></p></div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-cff154e6-f69f-44c8-9309-364cbe0b697e"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-cff154e6-f69f-44c8-9309-364cbe0b697e" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-cff154e6-f69f-44c8-9309-364cbe0b697e">
            What is conformity assessment?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-cff154e6-f69f-44c8-9309-364cbe0b697e" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-cff154e6-f69f-44c8-9309-364cbe0b697e" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Conformity assessment involves a set of processes that show your product, service or system meets the requirements of a standard. It's important to note that ISO doesn’t provide certification or conformity assessment. Find out more <a href="/conformity-assessment.html" title="Certification & conformity">about conformity assessment</a>.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-73cb37cd-f734-4207-b6ab-8014884672f0"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-73cb37cd-f734-4207-b6ab-8014884672f0" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-73cb37cd-f734-4207-b6ab-8014884672f0">
            Does ISO carry out certification?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-73cb37cd-f734-4207-b6ab-8014884672f0" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-73cb37cd-f734-4207-b6ab-8014884672f0" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>No. ISO doesn’t provide certification or conformity assessment. Find out more about <a href="/conformity-assessment.html" title="Certification & conformity">how conformity assessment and certification works</a>.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-c0cfb08b-6c09-40b7-a3bc-67c502502ab5"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-c0cfb08b-6c09-40b7-a3bc-67c502502ab5" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-c0cfb08b-6c09-40b7-a3bc-67c502502ab5">
            Can I use the ISO logo?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-c0cfb08b-6c09-40b7-a3bc-67c502502ab5" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-c0cfb08b-6c09-40b7-a3bc-67c502502ab5" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Only ISO, ISO members, and ISO technical committees (TCs) are allowed to use the ISO logo and ISO short name in accordance with ISO Policies.  Read more about <a href="/iso-name-and-logo.html" title="ISO name and logo">our name and logo</a>.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-3b2241b5-2d4a-422e-b9e5-54f14baf713f"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-3b2241b5-2d4a-422e-b9e5-54f14baf713f" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-3b2241b5-2d4a-422e-b9e5-54f14baf713f">
            How can I find a certification body?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-3b2241b5-2d4a-422e-b9e5-54f14baf713f" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-3b2241b5-2d4a-422e-b9e5-54f14baf713f" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>At ISO we are not involved in certification, and do not issue certificates. However, we have created some useful information on how to <a href="/certification.html" title="Certification">verify a certification body</a>.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-04384188-d0bb-47ac-a6bf-012eeab9a8fc"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-04384188-d0bb-47ac-a6bf-012eeab9a8fc" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-04384188-d0bb-47ac-a6bf-012eeab9a8fc">
            How can I find out which standards are equivalent to ISO standards?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-04384188-d0bb-47ac-a6bf-012eeab9a8fc" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-04384188-d0bb-47ac-a6bf-012eeab9a8fc" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>ISO itself does not have data on equivalent standards (such as national or regional standards). However, a number of ISO members are able to provide this information. Therefore, <a href="/about/members" title="Members">please contact the ISO member in your country</a>.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-0b8bbebe-0fec-4265-ba22-0ac4ea2e0e78"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-0b8bbebe-0fec-4265-ba22-0ac4ea2e0e78" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-0b8bbebe-0fec-4265-ba22-0ac4ea2e0e78">
            How does ISO decide what standards to develop?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-0b8bbebe-0fec-4265-ba22-0ac4ea2e0e78" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-0b8bbebe-0fec-4265-ba22-0ac4ea2e0e78" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Working through the ISO community, it is the people who need the standards that decide. A particular industry or business sector can communicate its need for a standard to their national ISO member; the idea is then proposed to ISO as a whole.</p>

<p>If accepted, the project is assigned to an existing technical committee. Proposals may also be made to establish technical committees to cover new scopes of technological activity. In order to use resources most efficiently, ISO only develops new standards for which there are clear market requirements.</p>

<p>If you feel there is a need for a standard in your sector, <a href="/about/members" title="Members">please contact your ISO member</a>.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-12f75dc9-8cd9-4b09-9add-bb100399f94e"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-12f75dc9-8cd9-4b09-9add-bb100399f94e" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-12f75dc9-8cd9-4b09-9add-bb100399f94e">
            Why is there a charge for standards?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-12f75dc9-8cd9-4b09-9add-bb100399f94e" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-12f75dc9-8cd9-4b09-9add-bb100399f94e" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Developing, publishing and maintaining ISO standards incurs a cost, and revenues from selling them helps ISO and its members to cover an important part of these costs. Charging for standards allows us to ensure that they are developed in an impartial environment and therefore meet the needs of all stakeholders for which the standard is relevant. This is essential if standards are to remain effective in the real world. ISO and its members offer a number of options to access ISO standards. Contact us or <a href="/about/members" title="Members">your national ISO member</a> to find the best option for your needs.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-f7edbed7-419d-4fa5-b2f8-2581ea348921"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-f7edbed7-419d-4fa5-b2f8-2581ea348921" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-f7edbed7-419d-4fa5-b2f8-2581ea348921">
            What is ISO's relation to governments?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-f7edbed7-419d-4fa5-b2f8-2581ea348921" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-f7edbed7-419d-4fa5-b2f8-2581ea348921" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>ISO is a non-governmental organization (NGO). Therefore, unlike the United Nations, the national members of ISO are not delegations of the governments of those countries. Our national members are the national standards bodies, or equivalent organizations, in their country. Some of them are wholly private sector in origin, others are private sector organizations but have a special mandate from their governments on matters related to standardization, and others are part of the governmental framework of their countries. In addition, government experts often participate in ISO's standards' development work. So, while ISO is an NGO, it receives input from the public sector as it does from the private sector.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-fea48503-f250-4d8b-8d34-b7f4a6d52610"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-fea48503-f250-4d8b-8d34-b7f4a6d52610" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-fea48503-f250-4d8b-8d34-b7f4a6d52610">
            Who pays for ISO?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-fea48503-f250-4d8b-8d34-b7f4a6d52610" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-fea48503-f250-4d8b-8d34-b7f4a6d52610" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <div><a href="/about/members" title="Members">ISO's national members</a> pay subscriptions that meet the operational cost of ISO's Central Secretariat. The dues paid by each member are calculated as a proportion of their country's Gross National Product and trade figures. Another source of revenue is the sale of standards, which contributes more than a third of the budget.</div>

<div> </div>

<div>The operations of the Central Secretariat in Geneva represent only about one fifth of the cost of our international standardizing activities . The remaining costs are borne by the organizations which manage the specific projects or loan experts to participate in the technical work. These organizations are, in effect, subsidizing the technical work by paying the travel costs of the experts and allowing them time to work on their ISO assignments. Such organizations and individuals make an essential and highly valued contribution to standardization.</div>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-1d345079-53a2-45be-96ec-b3c5cfca2df5"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-1d345079-53a2-45be-96ec-b3c5cfca2df5" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-1d345079-53a2-45be-96ec-b3c5cfca2df5">
            Who runs ISO?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-1d345079-53a2-45be-96ec-b3c5cfca2df5" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-1d345079-53a2-45be-96ec-b3c5cfca2df5" data-bs-parent="#id-d4934b6b-8b9f-4372-9ee6-21c9e73499bf">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <div>The General Assembly is the ultimate authority of the Organization. It is composed of <a href="/about/members" title="Members">ISO members</a>, and considers any matter submitted by <a href="/committee/55010.html" style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);" title="ISO/COUNCIL">the ISO Council</a>. </div>

<div> </div>

<div>The proposals put to the General Assembly are developed by the Council,  which is drawn from the ISO membership. The Council, which resembles the board of directors of a business organization, meets three times per year to discuss key matters relating to ISO strategy and policy, financial as well as operational and statutory matters. ISO Council membership rotates regularly to ensure that it is representative.</div>

<div> </div>

<div>Operations are managed by a Secretary-General, who is appointed for five-year term. The Secretary-General reports to a President who is a prominent figure in standardization or in business, elected for two, or three years. To learn more, <a href="/structure.html" title="Structure">see our section on structure and governance</a>.</div>

<div> </div>

<div>While we work together with United Nations (UN) specialized agencies on some standardization projects, ISO is an independent not-for-profit organization and is not part of the UN.</div>
</div>
    </div>
</div></div>

</div><div class="collapse-link">
        <button class="accordion-button h2 collapsed" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#accordion-6c276e65-0e85-4f50-a6d7-a6d63fcf2a19" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordion-6c276e65-0e85-4f50-a6d7-a6d63fcf2a19">Purchasing</button>
    </div>
    <div class="collapse ms-4" id="accordion-6c276e65-0e85-4f50-a6d7-a6d63fcf2a19">
<div class="accordion  faqs" id="id-6c276e65-0e85-4f50-a6d7-a6d63fcf2a19">
    <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-922d43cd-7d20-4ebf-bb69-50b1d8adecbe"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-922d43cd-7d20-4ebf-bb69-50b1d8adecbe" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-922d43cd-7d20-4ebf-bb69-50b1d8adecbe">
            How can I purchase ISO products?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-922d43cd-7d20-4ebf-bb69-50b1d8adecbe" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-922d43cd-7d20-4ebf-bb69-50b1d8adecbe" data-bs-parent="#id-6c276e65-0e85-4f50-a6d7-a6d63fcf2a19">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Our ISO products can be purchased either from the <a href="/store.html" title="Store">ISO Store</a> or from the ISO national <a href="/about/members" title="Members">member body</a>. ISO Store All items available for purchase have an associated shopping basket function on the right side of the page. Here, you can choose the format (Paper, PDF and ePub) and the language of the publication.</p>

<p><strong>ISO Member:</strong></p>

<p>Orders for ISO Standards and other ISO Publications can be addressed to your national  ISO Member. Some members can offer a personalized service and give technical feedback on certain standards. The main benefit of ordering through your national member is that with them, you can purchase ISO Products in your local currency.</p>
</div>

    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-7a2de296-8c7e-4603-976c-57c9ba2aa85a"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-7a2de296-8c7e-4603-976c-57c9ba2aa85a" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-7a2de296-8c7e-4603-976c-57c9ba2aa85a">
            How can I purchase a withdrawn standard?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-7a2de296-8c7e-4603-976c-57c9ba2aa85a" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-7a2de296-8c7e-4603-976c-57c9ba2aa85a" data-bs-parent="#id-341eeb7a-26f1-440d-9ab4-fa8f5b60111e">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Withdrawn standards are available for sale in PDF or paper version, for the price of CHF 67.00 (+ Shipping & Handling for the paper copy). Withdrawn standards can only be purchased by contacting the ISO Customer Care Team, Opening Hours: Monday to Friday, from 9:00 to 12:00 and from 14:00 to 17:00 (UTC +1).</p>

<ul>
	<li>Phone: +41 22 749 08 88</li>
	<li>Email:  customerservice@iso.org</li>
</ul>

<p>Or by contacting your national <a href="/about/members" title="Members">ISO member</a> directly.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-9c7aea9f-ad57-4fd3-9a83-72c09e4f5d89"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-9c7aea9f-ad57-4fd3-9a83-72c09e4f5d89" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-9c7aea9f-ad57-4fd3-9a83-72c09e4f5d89">
            I want to purchase a corrigenda, but it is not available on the ISO Store?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-9c7aea9f-ad57-4fd3-9a83-72c09e4f5d89" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-9c7aea9f-ad57-4fd3-9a83-72c09e4f5d89" data-bs-parent="#id-341eeb7a-26f1-440d-9ab4-fa8f5b60111e">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>If you have purchased a standard and a corrigenda has been published, it will automatically be added to your Account. Alternatively, you can access it for free on the <a href="https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/" target="_blank">Online Browsing Platform</a>.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-5272bf95-c823-41b6-af59-e31498d5a1e3"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-5272bf95-c823-41b6-af59-e31498d5a1e3" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-5272bf95-c823-41b6-af59-e31498d5a1e3">
            If I purchase a Draft, will I get the final publication for free?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-5272bf95-c823-41b6-af59-e31498d5a1e3" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-5272bf95-c823-41b6-af59-e31498d5a1e3" data-bs-parent="#id-341eeb7a-26f1-440d-9ab4-fa8f5b60111e">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Purchasing the Draft version of a standard (ISO/DIS) doesn't grant you to have its final version for free. Draft versions are subject to changes, hence the final publication will have to be purchased as well.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-30068de6-a4ce-4146-ba7d-c5ca5914f173"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-30068de6-a4ce-4146-ba7d-c5ca5914f173" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-30068de6-a4ce-4146-ba7d-c5ca5914f173">
            What is a Redline document?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-30068de6-a4ce-4146-ba7d-c5ca5914f173" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-30068de6-a4ce-4146-ba7d-c5ca5914f173" data-bs-parent="#id-341eeb7a-26f1-440d-9ab4-fa8f5b60111e">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>A Redline document compares the current standard with the previous edition. It allows you to see any updates made at a glance, by highlighting in red, all the parts that were removed from the previous edition, and by highlighting in green the new parts that were added. Redline documents are not sold separately but as a bundle, included with the standard.</p>

<p>Information: Redline documents are only available for some standards.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-a5601748-d884-4aa1-a016-0884d193f1ca"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-a5601748-d884-4aa1-a016-0884d193f1ca" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-a5601748-d884-4aa1-a016-0884d193f1ca">
            Can I post the standard I have purchased on the intranet?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-a5601748-d884-4aa1-a016-0884d193f1ca" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-a5601748-d884-4aa1-a016-0884d193f1ca" data-bs-parent="#id-341eeb7a-26f1-440d-9ab4-fa8f5b60111e">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>As indicated in our <a href="/home/store/terms-conditions-licence-agreeme.html#Customer-Licence" title="Licence Agreement">Licence Agreement</a>, standards cannot be shared with other users or posted on a company intranet. If you wish to do so, please contact your national  <a href="/about/members" title="Members">ISO member</a>, who will be able to offer a suitable licence.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div></div>

</div><div class="collapse-link">
        <button class="accordion-button h2 collapsed" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#accordion-0096eb58-9e59-4680-99a7-ecfc1b824c41" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordion-0096eb58-9e59-4680-99a7-ecfc1b824c41">Country codes collection</button>
    </div>
    <div class="collapse ms-4" id="accordion-0096eb58-9e59-4680-99a7-ecfc1b824c41">
<div class="accordion  faqs" id="id-0096eb58-9e59-4680-99a7-ecfc1b824c41">
    <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-85771fa6-ced3-461a-9be1-592b5ec6a7af"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-85771fa6-ced3-461a-9be1-592b5ec6a7af" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-85771fa6-ced3-461a-9be1-592b5ec6a7af">
            What is a country codes collection and why purchase it?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-85771fa6-ced3-461a-9be1-592b5ec6a7af" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-85771fa6-ced3-461a-9be1-592b5ec6a7af" data-bs-parent="#id-0096eb58-9e59-4680-99a7-ecfc1b824c41">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>The  country codes collection is an annual subscription that provides you with the complete updated lists of official country codes from ISO 3166 (parts 1, 2 and 3) in .XML, .CSV and .XLS format so you can download them to your database. With the subscription you will also receive notifications of any updates.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-82b1b9b2-ea5c-4d57-ad07-cbeb1f9887e5"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-82b1b9b2-ea5c-4d57-ad07-cbeb1f9887e5" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-82b1b9b2-ea5c-4d57-ad07-cbeb1f9887e5">
            How do I download the country codes collection that I have purchased?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-82b1b9b2-ea5c-4d57-ad07-cbeb1f9887e5" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-82b1b9b2-ea5c-4d57-ad07-cbeb1f9887e5" data-bs-parent="#id-0096eb58-9e59-4680-99a7-ecfc1b824c41">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>You have to go to the <a href="https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/" target="_blank">Online Browsing Platform</a> and access to your Account. You will find your collection under the "Subscriptions" tab.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-7e83e040-4d9f-4ba4-943a-3927c1bb9d23"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-7e83e040-4d9f-4ba4-943a-3927c1bb9d23" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-7e83e040-4d9f-4ba4-943a-3927c1bb9d23">
            What can I do with the country codes collection that I have purchased?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-7e83e040-4d9f-4ba4-943a-3927c1bb9d23" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-7e83e040-4d9f-4ba4-943a-3927c1bb9d23" data-bs-parent="#id-0096eb58-9e59-4680-99a7-ecfc1b824c41">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>The Country Codes can be downloaded to your database and used in order to implement the standard ISO 3166. However, selling them to others and further reproduction is not permitted.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-86a42a06-6c4c-4740-a9c2-69b477615bdb"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-86a42a06-6c4c-4740-a9c2-69b477615bdb" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-86a42a06-6c4c-4740-a9c2-69b477615bdb">
            Will I be notified of any updates made to the country codes collection?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-86a42a06-6c4c-4740-a9c2-69b477615bdb" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-86a42a06-6c4c-4740-a9c2-69b477615bdb" data-bs-parent="#id-0096eb58-9e59-4680-99a7-ecfc1b824c41">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Updates are included in your subscription. You will be notified when changes are made so you can download the latest versions.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-1d4c9ea9-017b-48c7-8c5e-44b2a46ef367"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-1d4c9ea9-017b-48c7-8c5e-44b2a46ef367" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-1d4c9ea9-017b-48c7-8c5e-44b2a46ef367">
            What happens when my country codes subscription expires?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-1d4c9ea9-017b-48c7-8c5e-44b2a46ef367" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-1d4c9ea9-017b-48c7-8c5e-44b2a46ef367" data-bs-parent="#id-0096eb58-9e59-4680-99a7-ecfc1b824c41">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Your subscription is automatically renewed every year, which means that you will keep receiving updates until you stop the auto-renewal. This is easy to do through from  your account and will be effective immediately.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div></div>

</div><div class="collapse-link">
        <button class="accordion-button h2 collapsed" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#accordion-a8e2347d-f47a-47c7-9a45-d13d6ad8f6a6" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordion-a8e2347d-f47a-47c7-9a45-d13d6ad8f6a6">Graphical symbols</button>
    </div>
    <div class="collapse ms-4" id="accordion-a8e2347d-f47a-47c7-9a45-d13d6ad8f6a6">
<div class="accordion  faqs" id="id-a8e2347d-f47a-47c7-9a45-d13d6ad8f6a6">
    <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-28440c69-9a31-4229-ac42-2051d8a0e0ef"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-28440c69-9a31-4229-ac42-2051d8a0e0ef" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-28440c69-9a31-4229-ac42-2051d8a0e0ef">
            How can I purchase Graphical Symbols?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-28440c69-9a31-4229-ac42-2051d8a0e0ef" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-28440c69-9a31-4229-ac42-2051d8a0e0ef" data-bs-parent="#id-a8e2347d-f47a-47c7-9a45-d13d6ad8f6a6">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>If you are looking for a single Graphical Symbol, you can search, preview and buy it from the <a href="https://www.iso.org/obp/ui" target="_blank"> Online Browsing Platform</a> (OBP). They are available in AI, DWG, EPS formats and in some cases also in vectorized PDF. If you buy a Graphical Symbol collection, (<a href="/publication/PUB400001.html" title="PUB400001 - ISO 7000 Graphical symbols for use on equipment">ISO 7000</a> or <a href="/publication/PUB400008.html" title="PUB400008 - ISO 7000 / IEC 60417 Graphical symbols for use on equipment">ISO 7000/IEC 60417</a>), you pay a yearly fee to access and download the symbols.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-55adb2da-4de8-4622-ba8b-f1438d4d7ff7"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-55adb2da-4de8-4622-ba8b-f1438d4d7ff7" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-55adb2da-4de8-4622-ba8b-f1438d4d7ff7">
            How do I access the Graphical Symbols that I have purchased?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-55adb2da-4de8-4622-ba8b-f1438d4d7ff7" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-55adb2da-4de8-4622-ba8b-f1438d4d7ff7" data-bs-parent="#id-a8e2347d-f47a-47c7-9a45-d13d6ad8f6a6">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>You have to go to the <a href="https://www.iso.org/obp/ui" target="_blank">Online Browsing Platform</a>  and log into your Account. If you purchased an individual symbol, it will be available under the "Products" tab. If you purchased a Collection of Graphical Symbols, you will find it under the "Subscriptions" tab.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-505e9ee6-29c0-48e0-91a0-9a735825236b"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-505e9ee6-29c0-48e0-91a0-9a735825236b" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-505e9ee6-29c0-48e0-91a0-9a735825236b">
            What can I do with the Graphical Symbols that I have purchased?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-505e9ee6-29c0-48e0-91a0-9a735825236b" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-505e9ee6-29c0-48e0-91a0-9a735825236b" data-bs-parent="#id-a8e2347d-f47a-47c7-9a45-d13d6ad8f6a6">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>Graphical Symbols can be reproduced as needed for the implementation of the respective ISO Standards. However, posting them on the Internet or selling them to others is not permitted.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-bf0da97f-2036-40a3-9c06-b0231e731f7a"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-bf0da97f-2036-40a3-9c06-b0231e731f7a" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-bf0da97f-2036-40a3-9c06-b0231e731f7a">
            Will I be notified of any updates made to the Graphical Symbols Collection?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-bf0da97f-2036-40a3-9c06-b0231e731f7a" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-bf0da97f-2036-40a3-9c06-b0231e731f7a" data-bs-parent="#id-a8e2347d-f47a-47c7-9a45-d13d6ad8f6a6">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>When you subscribe to a Graphical Symbol Collection, you will be informed if an update is available. Updates are included in your annual subscription and any modification in the collection will be updated automatically in your Account, free of charge.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-a6fef486-4a22-4489-9ef7-0cd359f23f52"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-a6fef486-4a22-4489-9ef7-0cd359f23f52" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-a6fef486-4a22-4489-9ef7-0cd359f23f52">
            What happens when my subscription expires?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-a6fef486-4a22-4489-9ef7-0cd359f23f52" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-a6fef486-4a22-4489-9ef7-0cd359f23f52" data-bs-parent="#id-a8e2347d-f47a-47c7-9a45-d13d6ad8f6a6">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>The subscription to a Graphical Symbols Collection lasts for one year. The subscription is automatically renewed, unless you cancel the renewal. To do so, you have to log into your Account and select the "Stop Auto-renewal".</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div></div>

</div><div class="collapse-link">
        <button class="accordion-button h2 collapsed" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#accordion-2493eacf-42a9-44a9-8dd8-c60b13d9e7d8" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordion-2493eacf-42a9-44a9-8dd8-c60b13d9e7d8">Newsletter & notification tool</button>
    </div>
    <div class="collapse ms-4" id="accordion-2493eacf-42a9-44a9-8dd8-c60b13d9e7d8">
<div class="accordion  faqs" id="id-2493eacf-42a9-44a9-8dd8-c60b13d9e7d8">
    <div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-6365d557-e067-4913-b2d5-b85928dc8798"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-6365d557-e067-4913-b2d5-b85928dc8798" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-6365d557-e067-4913-b2d5-b85928dc8798">
            What is the notification tool?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-6365d557-e067-4913-b2d5-b85928dc8798" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-6365d557-e067-4913-b2d5-b85928dc8798" data-bs-parent="#id-2493eacf-42a9-44a9-8dd8-c60b13d9e7d8">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>The notification tool sends you an alert via email when there is any updated information regarding a standard you follow. You will receive information when a new standard is published, withdrawn, or if a new format of the standard is available.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-b4ea70db-919c-44ec-8586-d44ece6aeaea"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-b4ea70db-919c-44ec-8586-d44ece6aeaea" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-b4ea70db-919c-44ec-8586-d44ece6aeaea">
            How can I subscribe to notifications?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-b4ea70db-919c-44ec-8586-d44ece6aeaea" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-b4ea70db-919c-44ec-8586-d44ece6aeaea" data-bs-parent="#id-2493eacf-42a9-44a9-8dd8-c60b13d9e7d8">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>First of all, you will need to sign into your Account. Then you can go to the  Online Browsing Platform, search for the standard and click on "Follow". If you wish to stop following a standard, then you go to your Account and uncheck the "Following" button. Another possibility is when you buy a standard through the ISO Store. On the Shopping Basket, the "Follow" function will be automatically selected. If you do not want to receive notifications about the standard, you can uncheck "Follow".</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div><div class="accordion-item">
    <h2 class="accordion-header" id="heading-6829cd40-48d0-421b-adcb-9fa799f91edc"><button class="accordion-button  collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#id-6829cd40-48d0-421b-adcb-9fa799f91edc" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="id-6829cd40-48d0-421b-adcb-9fa799f91edc">
            How can I access the documents from the notifications?</button>
        </h2><div id="id-6829cd40-48d0-421b-adcb-9fa799f91edc" class="accordion-collapse collapse " aria-labelledby="heading-6829cd40-48d0-421b-adcb-9fa799f91edc" data-bs-parent="#id-2493eacf-42a9-44a9-8dd8-c60b13d9e7d8">
        <div class="accordion-body">
            <p>You can click on the document reference to access it. If it is already part of your library, you will be able to see the entire document. Otherwise, you will only be able to see the publicly available sections. You can then decide to purchase the standard if you wish.</p>
</div>
    </div>
</div></div>

<h6><a href="/casco.html" title="CASCO">CASCO</a> (Conformity Assessment Committee):</h6>

<p>Committee whose secretariat is provided by ISO/CS that deals with conformity assessment and is responsible for the development of conformity assessment standards.</p>

Individuals or businesses can't join ISO. Membership of ISO is only open to national standards institutes or similar organizations that represent standardization in their country (one member in each country). It's important to realize that companies that apply or certify ISO standards are not ISO members. Find out more about ISO members. What is conformity assessment? Conformity assessment involves a set of processes that show your product, service or system meets the requirements of a standard. It's important to note that ISO doesn’t provide certification or conformity assessment. Find out more about conformity assessment . Does ISO carry out certification? No. ISO doesn’t provide certification or conformity assessment. Find out more about how conformity assessment and certification works . Can I use the ISO logo? Only ISO, ISO members, and ISO technical committees (TCs) are allowed to use the ISO logo and ISO short name in accordance with ISO Policies.  Read more about our name and logo . How can I find a certification body? At ISO we are not involved in certification, and do not issue certificates. However, we have created some useful information on how to  verify a certification body . How can I find out which standards are equivalent to ISO standards? ISO itself does not have data on equivalent standards (such as national or regional standards). However, a number of ISO members are able to provide this information. Therefore, please contact the ISO member in your country . How does ISO decide what standards to develop? Working through the ISO community, it is the people who need the standards that decide. A particular industry or business sector can communicate its need for a standard to their national ISO member; the idea is then proposed to ISO as a whole. If accepted, the project is assigned to an existing technical committee. Proposals may also be made to establish technical committees to cover new scopes of technological activity. In order to use resources most efficiently, ISO only develops new standards for which there are clear market requirements. If you feel there is a need for a standard in your sector, please contact your ISO member . Why is there a charge for standards? Developing, publishing and maintaining ISO standards incurs a cost, and revenues from selling them helps ISO and its members to cover an important part of these costs. Charging for standards allows us to ensure that they are developed in an impartial environment and therefore meet the needs of all stakeholders for which the standard is relevant. This is essential if standards are to remain effective in the real world. ISO and its members offer a number of options to access ISO standards. Contact us or your national ISO member to find the best option for your needs. What is ISO's relation to governments? ISO is a non-governmental organization (NGO). Therefore, unlike the United Nations, the national members of ISO are not delegations of the governments of those countries. Our national members are the national standards bodies, or equivalent organizations, in their country. Some of them are wholly private sector in origin, others are private sector organizations but have a special mandate from their governments on matters related to standardization, and others are part of the governmental framework of their countries. In addition, government experts often participate in ISO's standards' development work. So, while ISO is an NGO, it receives input from the public sector as it does from the private sector. Who pays for ISO? ISO's national members pay subscriptions that meet the operational cost of ISO's Central Secretariat. The dues paid by each member are calculated as a proportion of their country's Gross National Product and trade figures. Another source of revenue is the sale of standards, which contributes more than a third of the budget.   The operations of the Central Secretariat in Geneva represent only about one fifth of the cost of our international standardizing activities . The remaining costs are borne by the organizations which manage the specific projects or loan experts to participate in the technical work. These organizations are, in effect, subsidizing the technical work by paying the travel costs of the experts and allowing them time to work on their ISO assignments. Such organizations and individuals make an essential and highly valued contribution to standardization. Who runs ISO? The General Assembly is the ultimate authority of the Organization. It is composed of ISO members , and considers any matter submitted by  the ISO Council .    The proposals put to the General Assembly are developed by the Council,  which is drawn from the ISO membership. The Council, which resembles the board of directors of a business organization, meets three times per year to discuss key matters relating to ISO strategy and policy, financial as well as operational and statutory matters. ISO Council membership rotates regularly to ensure that it is representative.   Operations are managed by a Secretary-General, who is appointed for five-year term. The Secretary-General reports to a President who is a prominent figure in standardization or in business, elected for two, or three years. To learn more, see our section on structure and governance .   While we work together with United Nations (UN) specialized agencies on some standardization projects, ISO is an independent not-for-profit organization and is not part of the UN. Purchasing How can I purchase ISO products? Our ISO products can be purchased either from the  ISO Store or from the ISO national member body . ISO Store All items available for purchase have an associated shopping basket function on the right side of the page. Here, you can choose the format (Paper, PDF and ePub) and the language of the publication. ISO Member: Orders for ISO Standards and other ISO Publications can be addressed to your national  ISO Member. Some members can offer a personalized service and give technical feedback on certain standards. The main benefit of ordering through your national member is that with them, you can purchase ISO Products in your local currency. What is the ISO Online Browsing Platform (OBP)? The Online Browsing Platform  is a platform created by ISO that allows you to search and access our standards online. On the OBP you can freely preview parts of the standards (Foreword, Introduction, Scope, Normative references or Terms & definitions). This can help you decide whether it is the right standard you are looking for. The OBP is also used to access and purchase Graphical Symbols & Symbol Collections, Country Codes, Terms & Definitions. Can I access the Online Browsing Platform (OBP) and my products offline? No, it is not possible to consult your library offline. But you can have offline access to any file you have previously downloaded to your computer. Can I pay in my local currency? What is CHF? Prices for ISO publications ordered from the ISO Store are expressed in Swiss Francs (CHF) and can only be invoiced in this currency. If you wish to convert the price of any ISO publication into your local currency, you can find a currency converter at  www.oanda.com . To purchase standards in your local currency, you can contact your national  ISO Member. Which payment methods are accepted by ISO? As our Terms & Conditions , you can pay for your order with a credit card (MasterCard, Visa, and American Express) or by bank transfer. No debit cards are accepted. Your credit card information will be secure with the use of our Secure Transaction System. (See also our Privacy Policy ). For payment by bank transfer, the payment must mention your order number. Note: All bank charges have to be paid by the purchaser. If you choose this payment method, you will receive an email with the bank information. Note: Please read carefully the terms of our License Agreement before placing your order.  How do I create or manage my Account? Creating an Account: Go to the Online Browsing Platform and click "Sign In" on the top right corner. Click "Create Account" and enter the information required. You will receive an email confirmation and will be asked to validate your account. Editing your Account Information: Go to your Account and click on "Profile". There you will be able to change the information you need. Note that this information is the one that will be displayed on your invoice, so make sure you keep it updated. The account is personal and the contact information needs to be properly indicated for a single user, and not a company. If you wish to modify the email address in your account, please contact the customer service.   How do I download my electronic documents? Once you have made the payment and received an order confirmation, the electronic document can be downloaded from your online account. You will find the document under the "Products" tab, where you can either view it online or download it to your computer. It is important to know that all electronic files are subject to   ISO Copyright , which you will need to comply with. How can I get an invoice for my purchase? Referring to our Terms & Conditions, if you need a copy of your invoice, you need to log into your Account. Under the "Orders tab", select your invoice and press the "Email" button. A copy will be sent to you by email. ISO regrets to inform you that once an order has been confirmed and an invoice has been generated, the invoice information can no longer be modified. Therefore please make sure that all the Account information is up to date.   When will I receive my shipment? As per our Terms & Conditions, if you purchased a product in CD or paper format , then it will be shipped to you according to your selected delivery method: Standard Delivery: 4-10 business days , no tracking possibilities Express Delivery (DHL): 2-4 business days, tracking number available Shipments are sent out from the ISO Central Secretariat in Switzerland, either on the same day or the next business day, after we receive your payment. Note: Shipments to Mexico will only by sent by Express delivery and shipments to Switzerland, only by Standard delivery. PDF files have to be downloaded directly from your online account: Go to your ISO Store account . What is the ISO Returns Policy? As per our Terms & Conditions, except in the case of an error made by the ISO Central Secretariat, ISO does not accept returns, nor provide a refund for PDF and ePub documents. For physical documents (paper or CD-ROM), the return has to be accepted by the ISO Central Secretariat first, who will explain the procedure to follow. Please note that orders will be credited only upon receipt of the returned goods. Information: Should you have any doubts about a standard you are interested in, you can refer to our Online Browsing Platform (OBP) where you can preview different sections of the standard free of charge. For more complete information, you can also contact our Customer Service team or the ISO member in your country.   Can I purchase a product that someone else is going to use? ISO publications come with a single-user licence. When you purchase a standard from the ISO Store, the document(s) can be assigned for your personal individual use (“You”) or for use by your colleague(s) (“someone else”) within your company. The document will be watermarked in the user’s name. If you wish to post standards on your company’s Intranet for access by multiple users, please  contact us  or your  ISO Member  to explore the options. Note: The ISO Store is dedicated to end users only and not resellers. If you are interested in reselling ISO products, please contact your national ISO Member for further information.   Standards and Handbooks How can I access the ISO Standards and Handbooks that I purchased? The electronic documents can be accessed from your Account . You will find the document under the "Products" tab, where you can either view it online on the   Online Browsing Platform (OBP)  or download it to your computer. It is important to know that all electronic files are subject to ISO Copyright , which you will need to comply with. For electronic files, you can store them on any device, and you are allowed to print one copy for your own personal needs. PDF files are provided in either character-based format or, for older documents, in TIFF image-based format. All PDF files purchased from the ISO Store are watermarked in order to protect  ISO Copyright. What is an ePub? ePub is short for "electronic publication". It is a format optimized for tablets, e-readers and smartphones. It allows you to easily navigate the publication on a small, touch screen. On iOS, you can download iBooks  from the AppStore for an optimized reading experience. All downloadable standards are watermarked. The ISO Central Secretariat uses watermarks in order to protect  ISO's Copyright . A watermark is additional information that has been added to a document to identify the rightful licensee of the document. Using a watermark is a means of personalizing each standard that you download. By default, the watermark in the PDF file displays (on each page of the document) the order number, the download date and the email address of the contact provided in the Account. A Redline document compares the current standard with the previous edition. It allows you to see any updates made at a glance, by highlighting in red, all the parts that were removed from the previous edition, and by highlighting in green the new parts that were added. Redline documents are not sold separately but as a bundle, included with the standard. Information: Redline documents are only available for some standards. If you wish to do so, please contact your national   ISO member , who will be able to offer a suitable licence. Country codes collection What is a country codes collection and why purchase it? The  country codes collection is an annual subscription that provides you with the complete updated lists of official country codes from ISO 3166 (parts 1, 2 and 3) in .XML, .CSV and .XLS format so you can download them to your database. With the subscription you will also receive notifications of any updates. How do I download the country codes collection that I have purchased? You have to go to the Online Browsing Platform and access to your Account. You will find your collection under the "Subscriptions" tab. However, selling them to others and further reproduction is not permitted. Will I be notified of any updates made to the country codes collection? Updates are included in your subscription. You will be notified when changes are made so you can download the latest versions. What happens when my country codes subscription expires? Your subscription is automatically renewed every year, which means that you will keep receiving updates until you stop the auto-renewal. This is easy to do through from  your account and will be effective immediately. Graphical symbols How can I purchase Graphical Symbols? If you are looking for a single Graphical Symbol, you can search, preview and buy it from the  Online Browsing Platform (OBP). They are available in AI, DWG, EPS formats and in some cases also in vectorized PDF. If you buy a Graphical Symbol collection, ( ISO 7000 or ISO 7000/IEC 60417 ), you pay a yearly fee to access and download the symbols. How do I access the Graphical Symbols that I have purchased? You have to go to the Online Browsing Platform  and log into your Account. If you purchased an individual symbol, it will be available under the "Products" tab. If you purchased a Collection of Graphical Symbols, you will find it under the "Subscriptions" tab. What can I do with the Graphical Symbols that I have purchased? Graphical Symbols can be reproduced as needed for the implementation of the respective ISO Standards. However, posting them on the Internet or selling them to others is not permitted. Will I be notified of any updates made to the Graphical Symbols Collection? When you subscribe to a Graphical Symbol Collection, you will be informed if an update is available. Updates are included in your annual subscription and any modification in the collection will be updated automatically in your Account, free of charge. What happens when my subscription expires? The subscription to a Graphical Symbols Collection lasts for one year. The subscription is automatically renewed, unless you cancel the renewal. To do so, you have to log into your Account and select the "Stop Auto-renewal". Newsletter & notification tool What is the notification tool? The notification tool sends you an alert via email when there is any updated information regarding a standard you follow. You will receive information when a new standard is published, withdrawn, or if a new format of the standard is available. How can I subscribe to notifications? First of all, you will need to sign into your Account. Then you can go to the  Online Browsing Platform, search for the standard and click on "Follow". If you wish to stop following a standard, then you go to your Account and uncheck the "Following" button. Another possibility is when you buy a standard through the ISO Store. On the Shopping Basket, the "Follow" function will be automatically selected. If you do not want to receive notifications about the standard, you can uncheck "Follow". How can I access the documents from the notifications? You can click on the document reference to access it. If it is already part of your library, you will be able to see the entire document. Otherwise, you will only be able to see the publicly available sections. You can then decide to purchase the standard if you wish. mainEntity.name: Can anyone join ISO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Individuals or businesses can't join ISO. Membership of ISO is only open to national standards institutes or similar organizations that represent standardization in their country (one member in each country). It's important to realize that companies that apply or certify ISO standards are not ISO members. Find out more about ISO members.

mainEntity.name: What is conformity assessment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Conformity assessment involves a set of processes that show your product, service or system meets the requirements of a standard. It's important to note that ISO doesn’t provide certification or conformity assessment. Find out more about conformity assessment.

mainEntity.name: Does ISO carry out certification?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. ISO doesn’t provide certification or conformity assessment. Find out more about how conformity assessment and certification works.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the ISO logo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only ISO, ISO members, and ISO technical committees (TCs) are allowed to use the ISO logo and ISO short name in accordance with ISO Policies.  Read more about our name and logo.

mainEntity.name: How can I find a certification body?

acceptedAnswer.text: At ISO we are not involved in certification, and do not issue certificates. However, we have created some useful information on how to verify a certification body.

mainEntity.name: How can I find out which standards are equivalent to ISO standards?

acceptedAnswer.text: ISO itself does not have data on equivalent standards (such as national or regional standards). However, a number of ISO members are able to provide this information. Therefore, please contact the ISO member in your country.

mainEntity.name: How does ISO decide what standards to develop?

acceptedAnswer.text: Working through the ISO community, it is the people who need the standards that decide. A particular industry or business sector can communicate its need for a standard to their national ISO member; the idea is then proposed to ISO as a whole. If accepted, the project is assigned to an existing technical committee. Proposals may also be made to establish technical committees to cover new scopes of technological activity. In order to use resources most efficiently, ISO only develops new standards for which there are clear market requirements. If you feel there is a need for a standard in your sector, please contact your ISO member.

mainEntity.name: Why is there a charge for standards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Developing, publishing and maintaining ISO standards incurs a cost, and revenues from selling them helps ISO and its members to cover an important part of these costs. Charging for standards allows us to ensure that they are developed in an impartial environment and therefore meet the needs of all stakeholders for which the standard is relevant. This is essential if standards are to remain effective in the real world. ISO and its members offer a number of options to access ISO standards. Contact us or your national ISO member to find the best option for your needs.

mainEntity.name: What is ISO's relation to governments?

acceptedAnswer.text: ISO is a non-governmental organization (NGO). Therefore, unlike the United Nations, the national members of ISO are not delegations of the governments of those countries. Our national members are the national standards bodies, or equivalent organizations, in their country. Some of them are wholly private sector in origin, others are private sector organizations but have a special mandate from their governments on matters related to standardization, and others are part of the governmental framework of their countries. In addition, government experts often participate in ISO's standards' development work. So, while ISO is an NGO, it receives input from the public sector as it does from the private sector.

mainEntity.name: Who pays for ISO?

acceptedAnswer.text: ISO's national members pay subscriptions that meet the operational cost of ISO's Central Secretariat. The dues paid by each member are calculated as a proportion of their country's Gross National Product and trade figures. Another source of revenue is the sale of standards, which contributes more than a third of the budget.   The operations of the Central Secretariat in Geneva represent only about one fifth of the cost of our international standardizing activities . The remaining costs are borne by the organizations which manage the specific projects or loan experts to participate in the technical work. These organizations are, in effect, subsidizing the technical work by paying the travel costs of the experts and allowing them time to work on their ISO assignments. Such organizations and individuals make an essential and highly valued contribution to standardization.

mainEntity.name: Who runs ISO?

acceptedAnswer.text: The General Assembly is the ultimate authority of the Organization. It is composed of ISO members, and considers any matter submitted by the ISO Council.    The proposals put to the General Assembly are developed by the Council,  which is drawn from the ISO membership. The Council, which resembles the board of directors of a business organization, meets three times per year to discuss key matters relating to ISO strategy and policy, financial as well as operational and statutory matters. ISO Council membership rotates regularly to ensure that it is representative.   Operations are managed by a Secretary-General, who is appointed for five-year term. The Secretary-General reports to a President who is a prominent figure in standardization or in business, elected for two, or three years. To learn more, see our section on structure and governance.   While we work together with United Nations (UN) specialized agencies on some standardization projects, ISO is an independent not-for-profit organization and is not part of the UN.

mainEntity.name: How can I purchase ISO products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our ISO products can be purchased either from the ISO Store or from the ISO national member body. ISO Store All items available for purchase have an associated shopping basket function on the right side of the page. Here, you can choose the format (Paper, PDF and ePub) and the language of the publication. ISO Member: Orders for ISO Standards and other ISO Publications can be addressed to your national  ISO Member. Some members can offer a personalized service and give technical feedback on certain standards. The main benefit of ordering through your national member is that with them, you can purchase ISO Products in your local currency.

mainEntity.name: What is the ISO Online Browsing Platform (OBP)?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Online Browsing Platform is a platform created by ISO that allows you to search and access our standards online. On the OBP you can freely preview parts of the standards (Foreword, Introduction, Scope, Normative references or Terms & definitions). This can help you decide whether it is the right standard you are looking for. The OBP is also used to access and purchase Graphical Symbols & Symbol Collections, Country Codes, Terms & Definitions.

mainEntity.name: Can I access the Online Browsing Platform (OBP) and my products offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, it is not possible to consult your library offline. But you can have offline access to any file you have previously downloaded to your computer.

mainEntity.name: Can I pay in my local currency? What is CHF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prices for ISO publications ordered from the ISO Store are expressed in Swiss Francs (CHF) and can only be invoiced in this currency. If you wish to convert the price of any ISO publication into your local currency, you can find a currency converter at www.oanda.com. To purchase standards in your local currency, you can contact your national  ISO Member.

mainEntity.name: Which payment methods are accepted by ISO?

acceptedAnswer.text: As our Terms & Conditions, you can pay for your order with a credit card (MasterCard, Visa, and American Express) or by bank transfer. No debit cards are accepted. Your credit card information will be secure with the use of our Secure Transaction System. (See also our Privacy Policy ). For payment by bank transfer, the payment must mention your order number. Note: All bank charges have to be paid by the purchaser. If you choose this payment method, you will receive an email with the bank information. Bank transfers can take around 3 working days to be processed.

mainEntity.name: What is ISO's Tax Policy?

acceptedAnswer.text: As per our Terms & Conditions, local taxes are applied to online orders delivered in Switzerland only. For international orders, no taxes are charged. If there are taxes to be paid outside of Switzerland, they are the customers' responsibility.

mainEntity.name: Who can purchase through the ISO Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ISO Store is dedicated to end users only and not resellers. If you are interested in reselling ISO products, please contact your national ISO Member for further information. Note: Please read carefully the terms of our License Agreement before placing your order.

mainEntity.name: How do I create or manage my Account?

acceptedAnswer.text: Creating an Account: Go to the Online Browsing Platform and click Sign In on the top right corner. Click Create Account and enter the information required. You will receive an email confirmation and will be asked to validate your account. Editing your Account Information: Go to your Account and click on Profile. There you will be able to change the information you need. Note that this information is the one that will be displayed on your invoice, so make sure you keep it updated. The account is personal and the contact information needs to be properly indicated for a single user, and not a company. If you wish to modify the email address in your account, please contact the customer service.

mainEntity.name: How do I download my electronic documents?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once you have made the payment and received an order confirmation, the electronic document can be downloaded from your online account. You will find the document under the Products tab, where you can either view it online or download it to your computer. It is important to know that all electronic files are subject to  ISO Copyright, which you will need to comply with.

mainEntity.name: How can I get an invoice for my purchase?

acceptedAnswer.text: Referring to our Terms & Conditions, if you need a copy of your invoice, you need to log into your Account. Under the Orders tab, select your invoice and press the Email button. A copy will be sent to you by email. ISO regrets to inform you that once an order has been confirmed and an invoice has been generated, the invoice information can no longer be modified. Therefore please make sure that all the Account information is up to date.

mainEntity.name: When will I receive my shipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: As per our Terms & Conditions, if you purchased a product in CD or paper format , then it will be shipped to you according to your selected delivery method: Standard Delivery: 4-10 business days , no tracking possibilities Express Delivery (DHL): 2-4 business days, tracking number available Shipments are sent out from the ISO Central Secretariat in Switzerland, either on the same day or the next business day, after we receive your payment. Note: Shipments to Mexico will only by sent by Express delivery and shipments to Switzerland, only by Standard delivery. PDF files have to be downloaded directly from your online account: Go to your ISO Store account.

mainEntity.name: What is the ISO Returns Policy?

acceptedAnswer.text: As per our Terms & Conditions, except in the case of an error made by the ISO Central Secretariat, ISO does not accept returns, nor provide a refund for PDF and ePub documents. For physical documents (paper or CD-ROM), the return has to be accepted by the ISO Central Secretariat first, who will explain the procedure to follow. Please note that orders will be credited only upon receipt of the returned goods. Information: Should you have any doubts about a standard you are interested in, you can refer to our Online Browsing Platform (OBP) where you can preview different sections of the standard free of charge. For more complete information, you can also contact our Customer Service team or the ISO member in your country.

mainEntity.name: Can I purchase a product that someone else is going to use?

acceptedAnswer.text: ISO publications come with a single-user licence. When you purchase a standard from the ISO Store, the document(s) can be assigned for your personal individual use (“You”) or for use by your colleague(s) (“someone else”) within your company. The document will be watermarked in the user’s name. If you wish to post standards on your company’s Intranet for access by multiple users, please contact us or your ISO Member to explore the options. Note: The ISO Store is dedicated to end users only and not resellers. If you are interested in reselling ISO products, please contact your national ISO Member for further information.

mainEntity.name: How can I access the ISO Standards and Handbooks that I purchased?

acceptedAnswer.text: The electronic documents can be accessed from your Account . You will find the document under the Products tab, where you can either view it online on the  Online Browsing Platform (OBP)  or download it to your computer. It is important to know that all electronic files are subject to ISO Copyright, which you will need to comply with. If you purchased a product in CD or paper format, then it will be shipped to you according to your selected delivery method: Standard Delivery : 4-10 business days, sent via standard mail, no tracking possibility, Express Delivery : 2-4 business days, sent via DHL with tracking number available Shipments are sent out from the ISO Central Secretariat in Switzerland, either on the same day or the next business day, after we receive your payment.

mainEntity.name: What can I do with the standard I have purchased?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you purchase a hardcopy, you are allowed to share it with any person that wants to read it. However, you cannot copy the text by scanning it, photocopying it, or reproducing it in any other way. For electronic files, you can store them on any device, and you are allowed to print one copy for your own personal needs. However, you are not allowed to make copies or transfer the electronic file, or reproduce parts of it. For more information, please contact us at  copyright@iso.org.

mainEntity.name: What is an Adobe Acrobat PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: PDF is a file format created by Adobe. In order to open and read the PDF files you have purchased you will need to have the  Acrobat Reader Software installed on your computer. PDF files are provided in either character-based format or, for older documents, in TIFF image-based format. All PDF files purchased from the ISO Store are watermarked in order to protect  ISO Copyright.

mainEntity.name: What is an ePub?

acceptedAnswer.text: ePub is short for electronic publication. It is a format optimized for tablets, e-readers and smartphones. It allows you to easily navigate the publication on a small, touch screen. On iOS, you can download iBooks from the AppStore for an optimized reading experience. To add the file to your Apple device, you can download the file from your Account and add it to the iTunes Library. For Android, you can download FBReader from Google Play.

mainEntity.name: What is a watermark?

acceptedAnswer.text: All downloadable standards are watermarked. The ISO Central Secretariat uses watermarks in order to protect  ISO's Copyright. A watermark is additional information that has been added to a document to identify the rightful licensee of the document. Using a watermark is a means of personalizing each standard that you download. By default, the watermark in the PDF file displays (on each page of the document) the order number, the download date and the email address of the contact provided in the Account.
